resources.string: With the phone closed, hold a volume button to open the outside-screen page (or switch the flashlight) you chose for it in LCD Clock; at first volume-down opens the timer and volume-up your Home Assistant buttons. Short presses still change the volume, and nothing happens while the phone is open.

Swipe up on the clock face. Tap one to read all of it on its own page; dismiss one with ×, or CLEAR them all. While the phone is locked they\'re restricted (just the app and its lock-screen text, whatever your lock screen is set to show); unlock with the fingerprint to see the rest.

Swipe down on the clock face. Choose and order the controls below. SOS flashes ··· ——— ··· with the flashlight until tapped again, even with the screen off or the phone locked. BEDTIME switches Digital Wellbeing\'s Bedtime mode on and off. Home Assistant and VPN work only while the phone is unlocked: tapping one while locked asks for your fingerprint, then switches it. Android doesn\'t let apps switch Wi-Fi, mobile data or Bluetooth.
With the phone closed and the outside screen on, hold a volume button for a moment to jump straight to a page, or to switch the flashlight. Short presses still change the volume.

Battery saver and Night Light need a permission Android only gives from a computer, once: with the phone connected over USB debugging, run\nadb shell pm grant dev.lcdclock android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS
The outside screen\'s clock face on your home screen
Uses WG Tunnel\'s remote control: turn on Remote control in WG Tunnel\'s advanced settings, then copy its key and your tunnel\'s name here.

Your razr\'s outside screen: the LCD Digits clock face, and the pages you swipe to from it.
The colour is chosen in Clock styles: four presets, or Motorola\'s custom colours.
LCD Digits is the clock style
Choose LCD Digits in Clock styles. If you already have, wake the outside screen once.
Lets volume holds and the clock face open the pages: turn on \"LCD Clock cover button\" in Accessibility.
Lets the music tabs see and control what\'s playing.
Microphone, calendar, location and audio files allowed
For the recorder (and other apps\' recordings in Recordings), calendar and weather pages, and the timer\'s notification.
In the order you swipe through them on the outside screen, after the clock face. Each has its own screen timeout.

LCD Clock\'s own copy of the face, put up when the outside screen wakes: swipe left or right for the pages, up or down for Motorola\'s face, panels and notifications. The padlock above the alarm bell is lit while the phone is locked; touch the fingerprint sensor to unlock, as on Motorola\'s face.

string-array.item: LCD Clock\'s own countdown timer: it keeps running with the screen off and rings on the outside screen.
A daily alarm: tap the bell to turn it on or off.
Your events for the next 7 days.
The forecast for your approximate location, from Open-Meteo.
LCD Clock\'s own recorder: records even with the screen off and the phone locked, saving to Recordings. Playing and LIST (every recording in Recordings) need the phone unlocked.

Your Home Assistant buttons. Set up its buttons below; it shows once one is set up. The buttons work only while the phone is unlocked: tapping one while locked asks for your fingerprint, then switches it.
A tab per app with music, showing the app\'s icon. Opens when music starts.

Three icon buttons on the outside screen\'s HOME page (a volume hold can open it; see Volume button holds). Each button runs its Home Assistant actions using the Home Assistant app\'s own login; add two actions to one button to toggle two things at once.

With a long-lived access token (Home Assistant → your profile → Security), each HOME icon lights while any of its entities is on, and tapping switches them all off, or all on. Buttons without entities keep using their widget actions.
